sources.title: Towards Effective Extraction and Evaluation of Factual Claims
sources.read_scope: Targeted full-text reading: §§2.1–2.3, 3.1–3.4, 4.1–4.2, 5.2–5.3, 6; §9 scope/annotator/hyperparameter limitations. Not all 50 pages or appendices.

findings.mechanism: Claimify separates sentence selection, disambiguation and decomposition. Context windows support reference resolution; unresolved ambiguity excludes the entire sentence. Evaluation separates entailment, element-level coverage and context-dependent verification outcomes.
findings.empirical: On BingCheck, sentence macro-F1 is 91.2%; element macro-F1 is 83.7%. Removing selection causes the largest ablation deterioration. Element evaluation retains 81% of sentences whose automated element-level verifiability agrees with sentence annotations.
findings.scope: Extraction quality on the paper's dataset and models; not downstream TabbyML correctness.

author_reported: Single dataset; three annotators; narrow windows can miss list preambles.
Disambiguation detection accuracy needs further evaluation.
our_inference: Dropping an entire ambiguous sentence can suppress unambiguous factual content. This cannot be copied as silent success under v4's coverage contract.
Automated element scoring and subset selection warrant independent validation.

verification.methods_results: Read source sections, not inferred from abstract. Reported numbers from §5.2; ablation interpretation from §6.

sources.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
sources.read_scope: Targeted PDF reading: §3.1 definition/assumptions, §4.2 estimator evaluation, limitations pp.12084–12085, Appendix B.2 segment-vs-system metrics. Other sections not fully read.

findings.mechanism: Break responses into one-information-unit facts and estimate the fraction supported by a designated knowledge source. Equal fact weighting and a sufficiently consistent source are explicit assumptions.
findings.empirical: The advertised <2% error concerns aggregate FActScore estimation, not 98% fact-level accuracy. §4.2 shows that a verifier better at individual judgments can yield a worse aggregate score because error directions differ.
findings.scope: Primarily biographies with Wikipedia; proof-of-concept extension is not broad domain validation.

author_reported: Nuanced, debatable facts and conflicting source collections violate important assumptions.
Estimator quality depends on generation distribution; precision omits recall.
our_inference: Selecting a verifier by generator identity is prohibited by this project's contract, even though the paper observes generator-dependent best estimators.
Atomic-count changes alter metric weights; a higher score alone cannot establish a better extractor.

verification.metadata: Title/year/venue/DOI checked against ACL; PDF uses Pang Wei Koh, while landing-page display says Pang Koh. Retained PDF name.
verification.methods_results: Aggregate-vs-individual distinction checked directly in §4.2 and B.2.

sources.title: VeriScore: Evaluating the factuality of verifiable claims in long-form text generation
sources.read_scope: Targeted PDF reading: §§2.1.1–2.1.2, §3.1 human extraction evaluation; full limitations. Did not fully read fine-tuning or all verification experiments.

findings.mechanism: Extract a single event/state with required modifiers, using the current sentence plus up to three previous and one following sentence. Verifiability filtering and reference resolution occur during extraction.
findings.empirical: Three raters assessed 120 texts (15 from each of eight sources), yielding 360 preferences; SAFE was preferred 26 times. The comparison used SAFE extraction plus revision, omitting its relevance stage.
findings.scope: Evidence for mixed-content extraction preference; not complete proposition recall or three-label grounding accuracy.

author_reported: Working verifiability definition, not a formal one; complex claims remain difficult.
Sliding-window extraction is slow; topic relevance is not judged.
our_inference: Its broad exclusion of advice/hypotheticals must not override v4's requirement to retain embedded factual premises.
A fixed sentence window may miss distant list headers or antecedents.

verification.metadata: ACL and PDF agree on title/authors/year; DOI from ACL.
verification.methods_results: Human-study sample and comparator conditions read in §3.1, not just the 93% abstract-level shorthand.

sources.title: Long-form factuality in large language models
sources.doi_note: Verified arXiv/DataCite DOI, not a conference DOI.
sources.read_scope: NeurIPS PDF §§2–4, §8; Appendix A.3, C.4–C.8 and beginning C.10. Not all 72 pages. Metadata cross-checked with arXiv v4 and DeepMind publication page.

findings.mechanism: SAFE splits sentences, resolves references, filters prompt relevance, and performs iterative web retrieval/verification. LongFact supplies open-domain long-answer prompts.
findings.empirical: The 72% agreement on 16,011 facts evaluates steps 2–4 using manually split inputs. C.4 separately measures extraction via response-level fact-count correlations (Pearson .798; Spearman .846), plus inspected examples.
findings.scope: Count correlation is not proposition recall or semantic equivalence. The 76% win rate is conditioned on 100 disagreements and researcher reannotation with broader web access.

author_reported: LLM reasoning/revision failures and search coverage failures remain.
Fact-level extraction alignment was not performed because wording differed.
our_inference: Web truth and prompt relevance filtering do not directly match v4's supplied-context, all-factual-assertions contract.

verification.metadata: NeurIPS PDF venue/title/authors confirmed; arXiv records v4 dated 2024-11-07 and DOI.
verification.methods_results: Main verification result and separate extraction evaluation checked in §4 and C.4.

sources.title: Decontextualization: Making Sentences Stand-Alone
sources.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics 9:447–461
sources.read_scope: Targeted PDF reading: §2 truth-conditional definition; §3.4 scope/sampling; §5.2 and Tables 4–5 automatic evaluation. Did not fully read human evaluation/downstream studies.

findings.mechanism: A decontextualized sentence must be interpretable alone while preserving its original truth-conditional meaning. Reference resolution, scoping and bridging are involved; implicatures are deliberately excluded.
findings.empirical: On the selected Wikipedia task, T5-11B outperforms the coreference baseline on reported SARI-add/delete scores. Exact match can reward unchanged copying; SARI is explicitly not an accuracy percentage.
findings.scope: English Wikipedia sentences selected to favor simple edits and low background-knowledge demands.

author_reported: News, literary/social contexts and technical domains are harder; valid rewrites and feasibility judgments can differ.
our_inference: Standalone readability alone cannot certify preservation of a scientific condition or numerical relation.
The paper's semantic definition should be distinguished from v4's broader implicit-factual-content policy.

sources.title: A Closer Look at Claim Decomposition
sources.read_scope: Targeted PDF reading: §§3.1–3.2; conclusion/limitations; Appendix Tables 3–6. Did not fully read every decomposition prompt.

findings.mechanism: DecompScore replaces the external evidence with the original sentence and counts supported subclaims per passage. Proposed examples draw on logical atomism and neo-Davidsonian semantics.
findings.empirical: Holding generated biographies fixed, changing decomposition changes FActScore; Table 4 macro-averages range from 24.1 to 35.3 across methods. Authors explicitly say a larger FActScore is not necessarily better extraction.
findings.scope: Biographies, English, particular decomposers/verifier; demonstrates measurement sensitivity.

author_reported: All tested methods still omit subclaims; many yield non-atomic units.
Only claimed content is evaluated, not relevant information omitted by the generator.
our_inference: Supported-subclaim counts can reward redundant/easy fragments unless coverage and redundancy are separately assessed.
A decomposition evaluator must not replace verification against supplied evidence.

verification.metadata: ACL metadata and PDF title/authors/year checked; DOI on ACL.
verification.methods_results: Definition directly checked in §3.2; numeric range verified in Table 4.

sources.title: Decomposition Dilemmas: Does Claim Decomposition Boost or Burden Fact-Checking Performance?
sources.read_scope: Targeted full-text reading: §3.2 pipeline/settings; §4 and Tables 1–3; §5 error taxonomy; §6 trade-off/complexity experiments; §8 limitations. Not all appendix material.

findings.mechanism: Compares three decomposition styles, multiple verifiers, claim/response granularities, retrieval and harmonic-mean aggregation. Errors include lost details/relations, ambiguity, excessive fragmentation and changed meaning.
findings.empirical: WICE with MiniCheck: baseline BAcc 80.01/F1 72.32 versus FactScore decomposition 71.11/59.90. On FELM, MiniCheck plus VeriScore improves F1 48.10→67.56; GPT-4o-mini plus FactScore lowers F1 71.56→54.34.
findings.scope: Evidence that decomposition effects interact with input granularity and verifier, not universally positive.

author_reported: Binary labels only; retrieval/decomposition noise not directly quantified; length/count are complexity proxies.
our_inference: The empirical trade-off does not justify benchmark-specific branching or a universal maximum claim count.
Effects mix decomposition, retrieval and aggregation, unlike fixed-context v4.

verification.metadata: ACL landing page and PDF agree; DOI verified.
verification.methods_results: Read methods, opposite-direction results, taxonomy and limitations directly; no abstract-derived numbers.

sources.title: DnDScore: Decontextualization and Decomposition for Factuality Verification in Long-Form Text Generation
sources.read_scope: Targeted full-text reading: §§3.3–4.2, 5.2–5.3, 6.1–6.2, end §6 duplicate analysis, limitations, Appendix C.3 human evaluation and related Tables 8–9. Not all prompts/appendices.

findings.mechanism: DnD emits paired atomic subclaims and contextualized forms in one call. DnDScore supplies both to a verifier, asking it to judge the specified subclaim using context rather than treating all added context as another assertion.
findings.empirical: Human checking uses 100 LFQA instances selected because subclaim/contextualized judgments flip. Sufficient-information judgments rise 54%→88%; DnDScore agreement is 76%, contextualized FActScore 77%.
findings.scope: Supports importance of disambiguating context on selected disagreements; not broad superiority in accuracy.

author_reported: English biographies/QA; static known source documents; opinions outside scope.
our_inference: Average factuality-score rises are measurement changes, not accuracy gains.
Context must preserve conditions while avoiding duplicate counting; source context is not itself verification evidence.

verification.metadata: Parent supplied DOI-linked ACL page; verified ACL/PDF title/authors/year/venue.
verification.methods_results: Paired representation read in §§3.3/4.2; conditioned sample and numbers from C.3.

sources.title: Harmful Factuality: LLMs Correcting What They Shouldn't
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata; PDF pp.896–904 including §3 perturbation methods, §4.4 outcome definitions, §5 selected results, §6 mitigation, §8 limitations. Shell PDF extraction used after web find errors; middle of p.900 output truncated, not claimed fully read.

findings.mechanism: Controlled entity substitutions test whether summarization, rephrasing and grounded QA restore world-correct entities instead of preserving supplied input. Outcomes distinguish correction, retention, dual presence and omission.
findings.empirical: For the tested GEP summarization setting, a source-only instruction approximately halves harmful-correction rates for GPT-4.1/GPT-4o. This is a bounded experimental finding, not a universal scaling law.
findings.scope: WikiEntities perturbations and selected OpenAI/Llama models; generation tasks rather than a dedicated claim-extraction benchmark.

author_reported: Single corpus; limited model families; mitigation limited to prompts.
our_inference: Entity occurrence categories do not fully certify semantic faithfulness.
v4 already prohibits correction; the paper does not prove stronger wording improves v4 or that source-only instructions are sufficient.
